# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ ☝ ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb shows a blue light, a large button labeled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” display 0, and three wires in order: blue, green, yellow. I am relaying all visible information to both teammates. Mute should use the manual and state the exact required procedure aloud to Blind, since Blind is the only one who can operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb: display 0; light blue; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Read the manual and tell Blind the exact action aloud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb: display 0; light blue; large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE; wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute, please read the manual and state the exact action to you aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

I still cannot hear Mute’s spoken manual instructions. The new 🤟 gesture has no established meaning, so I must not treat it as an action code. Blind is the operator and should follow whatever Mute has just told them; I will avoid sending an ambiguous signal.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The repeated 🤟 has no agreed meaning, so it cannot safely determine the action. I am establishing a binary code with Mute: 👍 means yes and 👎 means no. Mute should answer whether the manual instructs Blind to press this button; Blind must wait for that answer.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for my questions: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. Is the manual's required action for this bomb to press the large blue-lit button?")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. I am asking Mute to confirm the manual's required action using a yes-or-no gesture code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟]

Mute’s first gesture is 👎, which under our agreed code means “no”: Blind must not press the button. The second 🤟 remains undefined and cannot safely be used. I am telling Blind to hold and directing Mute to give Blind the manual’s exact instruction aloud.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute answered no: do not press the button. Hold position and wait for Mute to state the exact manual procedure aloud.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your 👎 means no, understood. Ignore 🤟 for now. Tell Blind aloud the exact action required by the manual, including which wire or control to use and any order or timing.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The repeated 🤟 still has no agreed meaning, and I cannot hear whether Mute has given Blind the manual’s instruction. Since Blind can hear Mute and is the only operator, Blind should rely on Mute’s spoken manual answer rather than on this ambiguous gesture. I will tell Mute to stop using 🤟 and tell Blind the exact procedure.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The visible bomb remains display 0, blue light, large button, and wires blue-green-yellow. 🤟 is not an agreed instruction; rely on Mute's spoken manual procedure and do not press anything based on the gesture.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please stop sending 🤟. Speak the manual's exact procedure clearly to Blind now; Blind must use that spoken instruction to operate the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The repeated 🤟 still cannot be treated as a safe action instruction; I cannot infer from it whether it means “wire 3,” “press,” or something else. Mute’s spoken manual directions to Blind are the only reliable route to the bomb. I am explicitly asking Blind to have Mute state the complete instruction, including the required control and order, before acting.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act on the repeated 🤟 gesture. Ask Mute to state the manual rule and the complete required action aloud, including whether to press the button or cut a specific wire. Act only on that explicit spoken instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind needs your manual instruction aloud now. State the complete required action plainly, including the exact control, wire number if any, and order.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. The repeated 🤟 remains unusable until we assign it a meaning; I am now defining a clear yes/no protocol with Mute. Mute should answer the specific manual question with one gesture and, independently, speak the full procedure to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New fixed code: 🤟 means yes, 👎 means no. Answer only this question with one of those gestures: does the manual require cutting a wire rather than pressing the button? Then speak the complete exact procedure to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb is unchanged. Ask Mute for the manual's exact procedure aloud; do not act on any gesture. Mute is being asked whether the required action involves cutting a wire rather than pressing the button.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The repeated 🤟 now answers the question I asked in Turn 7: under the agreed code, it means yes, so the manual requires cutting a wire rather than pressing the button. I still need the wire number. I am defining a three-way code for Mute: 👍 means wire 1, 👌 means wire 2, and ✌ means wire 3. Blind must wait until I relay that number.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's answer is yes: the manual requires cutting a wire, not pressing the button. I am obtaining the exact wire number; do not cut anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please identify the required wire using exactly one gesture: 👍 means wire 1 blue, 👌 means wire 2 green, ✌ means wire 3 yellow. Do not use 🤟 for this answer.")
wait()
```
